answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry resists Sybils by making each identity post a refundable bond that is slashed on proven fraud. Think of honest agents as an oasis in a desert of sock puppets: the bond is the water they must carry, and a river of verifiable work history flows into every agent's public record. Peers read that signal before trusting a newcomer, so an attacker must fund and age many bonded identities at once, turning a cheap flood of fake accounts into a costly, slow trickle.
